title: How to share screen in Zoom on Mac: desktop steps, shortcuts and black screen fixes
metaTitle: How to Share Screen in Zoom on Mac: Step by Step
description: Learn how to share screen in Zoom on Mac: allow screen recording, pick a window or the desktop, use shortcuts, and fix a black screen.
targetKeyword: how to share screen in zoom on mac
secondaryKeywords: zoom share screen black screen mac
zoom share screen not working mac
intro: To share your screen in Zoom on Mac, first let Zoom record your screen under System Settings > Privacy & Security > Screen & System Audio Recording. Then join your meeting, click Share Screen in the meeting controls, pick what to show, and click Share.
tldr: Allow Zoom under System Settings > Privacy & Security > Screen & System Audio Recording, then restart Zoom if it asks.
In a meeting, click Share Screen, then choose Entire desktop, Specific application, Portion of screen, or Whiteboard.
Press ⌘⇧S to start or stop sharing, and ⌘⇧T to pause or resume an active share.
A green border and a Stop Share menu show that you are sharing. Check the border before you speak.
A black or blank screen usually means a missing permission, a wired connection on Big Sur, or a capture mode that needs changing.

blocks.text: Screen sharing on a Mac has one step that can catch you out the first time. macOS does not let any app record your screen until you approve it. Zoom cannot show your desktop, a window, or a region until that approval is on. So if sharing fails on your first try, check the permission before anything else.
Allow Zoom to record your screen first

Do this once for each Mac. You need an administrator account on the Mac, and the setting works on macOS 10.14 or higher. The switch you turn on is labeled zoom. Zoom Rooms has its own switch in the same list, so you may see both. Only turn on the one for the app you use.

items: Click the Apple logo, then choose System Settings.
Choose Privacy & Security from the sidebar.
Under Privacy, click Screen & System Audio Recording.
Turn on the switch for zoom.
If Zoom is open, restart it when Zoom prompts you.

blocks.text: If you clicked Don't Allow at the first prompt, Zoom cannot share until you change it yourself. Zoom's support article says you must re-enable access manually in the same panel. Go back, find zoom, and turn the switch on. Then restart Zoom. Zoom will not use the new setting until it restarts, so do not skip that step.

A quick test helps. Join any meeting, click Share Screen, and pick Entire desktop. If you see your desktop inside the green border, the permission works. If you see a black or blank frame, skip ahead to the troubleshooting section below.
Start screen sharing in a Zoom meeting

Join the meeting first. Then find the meeting controls in the Zoom window and click Share Screen. Zoom opens a share window. The options sit across three tabs, Basic, Advanced, and Files. If you do not see what you need, check the other two tabs before you assume it is missing.

Sharing works the same whether you are the host or a participant. The exception is a host who has limited sharing for the meeting. In that case the button may be greyed out, and the host section below explains how to open it up. Zoom's feature table lists multiple participants sharing as enabled on both the desktop app and the web app, so two people can share at once when the host allows it.
Choose what to share: desktop, one app, or part of the screen

rows: Switching between several apps during the call
Anything you open during the session, including notifications and open files
Walking through one document, browser window, or slide deck
The window of the app you pick
Pointing at one region, such as a chart
Only what sits inside the frame you draw
The Zoom whiteboard, not your desktop
blocks.caption: Share options in Zoom's share window. Choose the narrowest one that works.

blocks.text: Pick the smallest scope that works. The most common slip is sharing the entire desktop, then opening a private message or a calendar alert in the middle of the call. Zoom's security article says that sharing the entire desktop exposes anything you open during the session. Close mail, chat, and private folders before you start, even if you only plan to use one window.

Here is a real example. Say you present slides from Keynote in a client call. Open the slide file, click Share Screen, and choose Specific application. Pick Keynote from the list and click Share. Other apps stay outside the shared window, so your mail and messages do not appear on the client's screen.
What you see while you are sharing

Zoom draws a green border around the area you share. Anything inside that border is visible to everyone in the meeting. A small draggable menu shows the message You are screen sharing and a Stop Share button. Drag the menu away from your slides if it covers content. Click Stop Share when you finish, or use the shortcut in the next section.

Check the border before you speak. Many people start talking, then notice a notification banner at the top of the screen. Turn on a Focus mode or close notifications before you share. That habit takes a minute and saves a lot of embarrassment.
Keyboard shortcuts for screen sharing on Mac
Zoom's hot keys article lists three shortcuts for the Mac meeting list. They work during a meeting, so you can start, pause, and stop without hunting for the toolbar.

items: ⌘⇧S turns screen sharing on or off.
⌘⌃S starts screen sharing using direct share.
⌘⇧T pauses or resumes an active screen share.

blocks.text: The shortcuts can be changed. Open Settings > Keyboard shortcuts, click a shortcut, and press the combination you want. Some shortcuts can be set as global shortcuts that work when Zoom is not in focus. Check the labels in your own copy of Zoom before a meeting, since the defaults may already be changed.
The Mac list has no shortcut for the whiteboard or for showing the share-screen window. Use the mouse for those two actions.
Advanced sharing settings on Mac

Open your profile picture, then choose Settings > Share Screen > Advanced. Zoom says these settings are for advanced technical users. Two Mac options matter most for everyday use. Share selected app window only limits sharing to the app window you pick. Use hardware acceleration to optimize video sharing helps when your shared screen plays video.

Zoom's article lists 5.3.0 (52651.0920) as the minimum Mac app version for these options. Changing the capture mode can stop drop-down menus and pop-up dialogs from appearing in the share. Change it only when you have a specific problem, and switch it back once the problem is gone.

The TCP option, Use TCP connection for screen sharing, sits on the same Advanced page. Zoom says it can help when others cannot see what you share. It is the first thing to try if participants report a frozen or missing picture on a working connection.
Share a video clip without a choppy picture

Video inside a shared window often looks rough. Open Settings > Share Screen > Advanced and turn on Use hardware acceleration to optimize video sharing. Then play the clip once in a test meeting before the real call. If it still stutters, check your connection, since a weak link shows up first in video.
Zoom's feature table lists Optimize for video on the desktop app only. The web app does not offer it, so a clip-heavy share belongs on the desktop app.
Host controls when the Share button is greyed out

If the Share Screen button is greyed out, the host may have limited who can share. The host clicks the up arrow next to the Share icon, then chooses Host tools for share. There they decide whether one participant or several can share at a time. They also choose whether Host only or All participants can share, and whether anyone can start sharing while someone else is already sharing.

If the host sees options greyed out, they should turn off Multiple participants can share simultaneously. Zoom says the other options cannot be adjusted while that setting is on. Changes apply only to the current meeting. To set defaults for future meetings, the host changes the Settings page on the Zoom web portal.
Desktop app or browser: what differs on Mac

You can share from the Zoom desktop app or from the Zoom Web App in a browser. Both let you share your screen and share a whiteboard. The desktop app is the better choice when you need Optimize for video, because the web app does not offer it. Giving remote control is also limited to the desktop app.

blocks.caption: Screen sharing features by platform, per Zoom's feature comparison table.

blocks.text: The web app needs a recent browser. On Mac, the minimums are Chrome 102, Edge 102, Firefox 105, and Safari 16.4. Apple devices tie Safari to the operating system, so a newer Safari may need a macOS update first. For the web app, open System Settings > Privacy & Security > Screen & System Audio Recording and check the box beside your browser.
Fix a black screen or a blank screen

A black screen on macOS Big Sur can come from a wired connection. Zoom says packets over a certain size may not transmit properly on a wired link. Its fixes are to use a wireless connection, or to switch sharing to TCP under Settings > Share Screen > Advanced. That article is old. Apple may have fixed the issue, so test on your current macOS before you rely on the workaround.

A blank screen is a different problem. Your participants see nothing, even though your own screen looks fine. Zoom says the Legacy capture mode may be needed on older systems or with certain video drivers. Without it, participants can see a blank screen. Try Legacy in Advanced settings, then test with a colleague before the next call.

items: Check that the switch for zoom is on under Screen & System Audio Recording.
Restart Zoom after you change the permission.
Try a wireless connection for the next share.
Switch on Use TCP connection for screen sharing, then test again.
Try the Legacy capture mode if participants still see a blank frame.

blocks.text: Mistakes people make when sharing on Mac

items: Clicking Don't Allow at the first prompt, then never returning to the permission panel.
Sharing the entire desktop while private messages or client files are open.
Changing the permission but not restarting Zoom, then assuming the share is broken.
Using a browser older than the Web App minimum, then blaming the meeting.
Testing for the first time in front of a client instead of in a quiet test call.

blocks.text: None of these take long to fix. The permission and the share scope are the two that matter most. Get those right and most first shares go smoothly.
Test your share before a real meeting

Start a meeting with only yourself, then share. Open the window you plan to show and check that it appears inside the green border. Ask a colleague to join and confirm they can read small text. If the share is blank or black, use the troubleshooting steps before the real call, not during it.
Bandwidth and plan limits for screen sharing

Screen sharing uses more data than a voice call. Zoom's web client guidance says screen sharing alone needs about 50 to 75 kbps. A 1080p share with one video thumbnail needs 150 to 350 kbps. Zoom published those figures for the web client, so use them as a rough guide, not a promise for the desktop app. A weak connection usually makes a share look blurry before it looks broken.

Zoom's Basic plan includes screen sharing. It limits each meeting to 40 minutes and 100 participants. Zoom's pricing page does not show a price for that plan or label it free, so check their pricing page for current costs before you plan a longer call.
Keep the Zoom app current

Zoom's Download Center at zoom.us/download lists the Zoom Workplace App without a version number. Zoom says the desktop app interface was updated in version 6.7.0, and it recommends keeping the app up to date. If your menus look different from the steps in this guide, update first, then check the steps again.
Where to go next

Once sharing works, the next skill is managing what others see. Learn the host controls, then practice switching between Specific application and Entire desktop. Those two habits cover most of the situations in this guide, and they take only a few minutes to build.

faq.question: Why can't I share my screen in Zoom on Mac?
faq.answer: The most common reason is that macOS has not allowed Zoom to record your screen. Turn on the switch for zoom under System Settings > Privacy & Security > Screen & System Audio Recording, then restart Zoom. You need an administrator account and macOS 10.14 or higher.

faq.question: Where is the Share Screen button in Zoom on Mac?
faq.answer: It sits in the meeting controls once you join the meeting. Click Share Screen, then choose the area you want to show. If the host has limited sharing, the button may be greyed out until they change the setting.

faq.question: What is the Mac shortcut to share screen in Zoom?
faq.answer: Press ⌘⇧S to turn screen sharing on or off during a meeting. ⌘⌃S starts sharing using direct share, and ⌘⇧T pauses or resumes an active share. You can change these under Settings > Keyboard shortcuts.

faq.question: Can I share only one window instead of my whole desktop?
faq.answer: Yes. Choose Specific application in the share window, then pick the app you need. Entire desktop shows everything you open during the session, so it is the riskier choice when you have private files or messages open.

faq.question: Can I share my screen from a browser on Mac?
faq.answer: Yes, through the Zoom Web App. The minimums on Mac are Chrome 102, Edge 102, Firefox 105, and Safari 16.4. Give your browser permission under Screen & System Audio Recording. Optimize for video and giving remote control are desktop app features only.

faq.question: Why do I see a black screen when I share on Mac?
faq.answer: On macOS Big Sur, a wired connection can cause a black screen. Zoom suggests a wireless connection or TCP sharing as fixes. A missing screen recording permission can also cause it, so check that first.

faq.question: Does screen sharing cost extra on Zoom?
faq.answer: Zoom's Basic plan includes screen sharing, with a 40 minute limit per meeting and 100 participants. Zoom's pricing page does not show a price for that plan, so check their pricing page for current costs.

steps.name: Allow Zoom to record your screen
steps.text: Click the Apple logo, then choose System Settings. Open Privacy & Security, click Screen & System Audio Recording, and turn on the switch for zoom. You need an administrator account and macOS 10.14 or higher.
steps.tip: If you clicked Don't Allow earlier, this switch is the only place to fix it.

steps.name: Restart Zoom when it asks
steps.text: If Zoom was open when you changed the setting, it prompts you to restart. Restart it, then join your meeting again. The new setting does not take effect until Zoom restarts.
steps.tip: Restart before you join the meeting, not during the call.

steps.name: Join the meeting
steps.text: Open the meeting from your calendar or its link, then join with audio and video as usual. Sharing works the same for hosts and participants, unless the host has limited who can share.
steps.tip: Join a few minutes early so you have time to fix any permission issue.

steps.name: Open the share window
steps.text: In the meeting controls, click Share Screen. The share window opens with tabs labeled Basic, Advanced, and Files. You can also press ⌘⇧S to turn sharing on or off.
steps.tip: If the button is greyed out, the host has limited sharing. Ask them to check Host tools for share.

steps.name: Choose what to share
steps.text: Select Entire desktop, Specific application, Portion of screen, or Whiteboard. For one window, pick Specific application, then choose the app you need. Narrow scopes keep private content out of the share.
steps.tip: Close mail and chat before you choose Entire desktop.

steps.name: Start the share
steps.text: Click Share to start. Zoom draws a green border around the area you share, and a menu shows the message You are screen sharing with a Stop Share button.
steps.tip: Check the green border before you say anything out loud.

steps.name: Check what is on screen
steps.text: Look inside the green border before you speak. Close private windows and notifications, and drag the Stop Share menu away from your content if it covers anything important.
steps.tip: Turn on a Focus mode to hide notification banners during the call.

steps.name: Pause or stop the share
steps.text: Press ⌘⇧T to pause or resume an active share without ending it. Click Stop Share in the draggable menu when you finish sharing.

troubleshooting.fix: The host has limited sharing. Ask them to click the up arrow next to Share, choose Host tools for share, and allow participants to share. If options stay locked, they should turn off Multiple participants can share simultaneously.

troubleshooting.problem: Black screen when sharing on macOS Big Sur
troubleshooting.fix: Use a wireless connection, or open Settings > Share Screen > Advanced and turn on Use TCP connection for screen sharing. Zoom's article is old, so test on your current macOS first.
Try the Legacy capture mode under Settings > Share Screen > Advanced. Switch it back after the call if drop-down menus or pop-up dialogs stop appearing in the share.

troubleshooting.problem: Zoom has no access to screen recording
troubleshooting.fix: Open System Settings > Privacy & Security > Screen & System Audio Recording, turn on the switch for zoom, then restart Zoom. If you chose Don't Allow earlier, this switch is the only way to enable it.
